subject: arcticOutpost

Category: Diorama.
Subject: arctic research outpost.
Style: Firewatch flat colour.

spec.name: Arctic Research Outpost
spec.description: A Firewatch-style flat-colour diorama of a small polar research station: a red-orange main cabin on stilts, a radio mast, a Quonset storage hut, a weather-instrument yard and a snow-drift base with sled and fuel drums.
spec.layout: A low snow plateau (an irregular faceted slab, 6 x 5 m, 0.3 m thick) forms the base. The main cabin sits left of centre (x -0.6) on short stilts, with its door and stairs facing +Z. A tall lattice radio mast stands at the back right (x 1.9, z -1.4). A curved Quonset hut sits at the back left. A weather yard (Stevenson screen, anemometer, snow stakes) sits at front right. A sled, fuel drums and crates sit at front left. Style: Firewatch flat colour. Warm sunset oranges and reds against cool blue-violet snow shadows. Every surface is one flat colour. Details such as windows, stripes, rivets and lights are separate small parts. Snow caps the roofs and top faces in near-white, and blue-lavender snow shadows go on lower faces.

parts.builds: The snow plateau: a faceted irregular slab made of stacked, overlapping prisms and wedges, snowTop on top and snowShade/snowDeep on the sides and the lower skirt. It has drift wedges against the cabin and hut walls, a packed-path strip in snowShade leading from the cabin door toward the yard, a few rock clusters (rock) at the rim, and small ice patches (ice). Footprints are tiny dark dents on the path.
parts.attaches: Its top face at y=0.3 is the floor for every other part, which sit on snowTop.

parts.builds: The main cabin: a 2.2 x 1.3 x 1.8 m box body in cabinRed with cabinDark vertical board seams as thin strips, on four timber stilts with cross braces. It has a cream trim band and corner posts, and a gable roof in roofGrey with a snowTop cap and a snowShade underside. A stovepipe chimney (metalDark) emits a small snow-white cap. The front door is timber with a windowGlow porthole and a handle. Timber stairs lead down to the snow, with a railing. Each side has two glowing windows (windowGlow) with cream frames and shutters in cabinDark. A lampRed beacon sits on the roof ridge, and an ink sign plate is above the door. A fuel pipe runs down one side.
parts.attaches: Stilts end on snowTop (y=0.3). The cabin floor is at the cabinFloor mount, and the stairs meet the door at cabinDoor and the snow.

parts.builds: The radio mast: a tapering lattice tower 4.4 m tall made of four slim legs, ring braces and diagonal rods in alternating mastOrange and mastWhite bands. At the top are a dish, whip antennas and a lampRed light. Guy wires of thin metal rods run to small snow anchors. Near the base is a small metal equipment box with a door and a cable running to the cabin. A concrete-look footing in snowShade sits at its base.
parts.attaches: Base at the mastBase mount on snowTop; the cable heads toward the cabin at x -0.6.

parts.builds: A Quonset storage hut: a half-cylinder lathe or stacked arc ribs in huttGreen, 1.8 m wide, 1.0 m tall and 1.6 m long, with horizontal corrugation lines as thin darker strips. A snowTop layer lies along the top and metalDark end walls carry a door with a handle and a small windowGlow slit. Timber skids sit underneath, with a lantern (windowGlow) by the door and a stack of crates (timber and timberDark) beside it. Snowdrift wedges sit at the sides.
parts.attaches: Sits on snowTop at the huttBase mount.

parts.builds: The weather and supply yard: a white Stevenson screen with louvers on legs, an anemometer on a pole (three cups spinning, a vane), snow stakes in alternating red and white bands, a sled with timber runners and a tarp-covered load (cabinDark, with rope), three fuel drums (drumBlue, drumYellow) with ring ribs and caps, a stack of two crates, and a small ice-drill tripod in metal. Each item has small details: bolts, labels (ink), and a lampRed marker flag.
parts.attaches: Everything rests on snowTop at the yardCenter and sledSpot mounts. The path from cabinDoor leads between them.

I'm planning the buildMast function, defining the mast as a box positioned at the base coordinates with specific dimensions for width, height, and depth, without any joints.

For the tower structure, I'm setting the height so it tops out around 4.3 units with a whip antenna extending to 4.6, keeping everything within the bounding box. Now I'm defining the tower's square cross-section legs with tapering width from a wider base to a narrower top, dividing them into alternating orange and white bays with horizontal connecting rings at each level for a low-poly radio tower look.

I'm adding zigzag diagonal braces within each face per bay using thinner rods for contrast, then settling on 6 bays with a top ring to stay within a budget of roughly 150 elements. I'm also adding a concrete footing slab and small pedestal blocks under each leg for the base.

Now I'm working out pedestal heights and leg embedment, adding small plates and bolts at the leg bottoms, then deciding to skip extra snow details on the footing and instead place small snow lumps at the anchors. I'm moving on to plan a platform near the top around y=3.9.

Still defining the dish geometry...

Computing the dish's horizontal offset and tilted axis direction for the lathe orientation, keeping the rim extents within the tower's bounding box. Then I'm adding a red lamp near the top of the pole, considering using the glow kit for an emissive effect around the lamp cage.

Still writing structure details...

Adding a platform railing with posts and rails, then a ladder on one face of the tower with rails and rungs spaced about every 0.25 units up to near the top.

Now I'm tallying the total piece budget: footing, pedestals, and plates come to 9, legs across 6 bays with alternating colors add 24 pieces, and rings at each bay boundary plus the base ring add roughly another 24-28 parts.

Adding diagonals brings the running total near 135, then I'm accounting for the ladder, platform, pole, lamp, whip antennas, yagi antenna with its boom and elements, dish with feed and bracket, guy wires with anchors, and finally the equipment box with its body, door, handle, vent, and legs—bringing the total piece count up to around 141.

I'm trimming where I can to stay within budget, cutting ladder rungs and merging the base ring into plates, landing around 130 pieces total. Now I'm positioning the guy wires running from the tower's upper corner down to ground anchors, each anchor getting a small snow mound and a dark metal eye bolt detail.

Placing the wire rods with thin metal cylinders stretching between those tower and anchor points, then I'm working out where the equipment box should sit relative to the cabin and ladder — leaning toward the tower's opposite side near the front corner offset.

I'm setting the box to sit directly on the snow with dark metal skids, adding a door on the face toward the cabin with a handle and small indicator light, and shaping a slightly oversized snow-capped roof. Then I'm routing a cable with a smooth curved sweep from the box down to the ground, plotting a few path points so it trails off toward the surrounding area.

I decide the cable should end around x=1.2 but disappear into a buried snow mound rather than terminate abruptly, which reads more naturally as if it continues underground toward the cabin. I'm also planning a conduit running up the tower alongside this cable.

Now I'm working out the geometry for a conduit rod connecting the box to the tower leg, trying to figure out which corner leg to route it along and how it should angle upward from the box's top edge.

Shifting to the tower structure itself, I'm setting up a width interpolation function tapering the lattice from a wide base to a narrow top, defining bay levels, and ordering corner offsets by sign pairs. I'm also planning snow caps on the platform and the right color hardware for the cabin wiring, then starting a helper function for drawing the diagonal rods between corners.

Now I'm working out the alternating diagonal pattern between corners at each bay level, and assigning colors so legs and rings use the bay's color while diagonals use an inverse shade, with special cases for the bottom and top rings.

Then I'm calculating the ladder geometry on the +z face—rail positions at x=±0.1, rung placement along y at regular intervals, and matching the z-height to the frame's curved profile so everything aligns with the corner legs.

Now I'm setting up the equipment pieces using box geometry placed directly in model space, plus the platform at the top with its dimensions and a small snow cap layered on top, making sure the ladder and corner posts still clear everything.

Still working through rails, pole, lamp, and antenna geometry...

Checking for clearances between the whips at the corners and the yagi boom/elements so nothing overlaps near the platform edges.

Now I'm computing the dish mounting bracket's geometry — figuring the rod connecting the tower leg to the dish center, working out the diagonal offset toward the corner leg so the dish bracket angle lines up correctly.

Adding the rim torus, feed horn assembly with rod and cone tip, then computing perpendicular side vectors to place two support struts from the rim to the feed horn tip...

Now I'm shaping the dish lathe outline to be more concave with front and back curve points, then adding guy wires from tower attachment points to ground anchors along with small turnbuckle details.

Still placing geometry details...

Working out the footing layers with a darker skirt and lighter slab, then nudging the equipment box's center and size so it clears the footing edge without overlapping.

Now I'm detailing the metal box itself—placing a darker recessed door panel on the -x face with a handle, adding a small indicator light and label plate, and considering thin ink-colored louver strips on the +z side.

Then I'm adding a snow-capped roof cap and conduit stub, and working out the cable that exits the box near the bottom of the -x face, routing it down to the ground with a catmull curve. Now I'm figuring out the conduit routing from the box's top up to the tower leg, mapping out the corner coordinates near the pedestal to connect the two points cleanly.

I'm checking whether this conduit path collides with the dish bracket and ladder at higher levels, deciding to shorten it and terminate into a small junction box before it reaches the conflict point at y 3.5.

Writing the conduit and box code...

Adding diagonal bracing between corners...

Now I'm importing the glow kit for indicator lights, then building the dish using lathe geometry for the reflector body and torus geometry for ring details, positioned via vectors and axis orientation. I'm considering small extras like a flag marker or label plate but deciding to skip most of them for simplicity, keeping just the essential structural details before finalizing.

Working through the door geometry, checking that the arched top clears the crate corners given the hut's curved wall profile, and settling on a door height around 0.68-0.7 with the arch radius matching the hut's overall curvature.

Adding a stovepipe vent with a snow cap on top, dark base rail skirting along the bottom sides, and faceted snowdrift wedges at the sides for environmental detail...

I realize the drift can't spread that far, so I'm narrowing the hut width to 1.7 and shrinking the drift overhang to 0.15 so it doesn't collide with the cabin geometry. Still writing shape helpers...

Working out the snow cap layering with a thicker ridge band in the middle and a few lump spheres on top for texture, plus overhanging ends so it drapes naturally over the ribs.

Finishing the slit frame with a slightly oversized metal border and glow, skipping a second porthole. Now positioning a lantern on a wall bracket, checking it clears the crates and fits within the arch's width at that height.

Designing the lantern itself with a hanging arm, glass cylinder glow, thin posts, cone top, and ring handle, then placing it so it clears the crate stack near the door.

I try reasoning out a placard with ink bars positioned on the angled side wall, but the orientation math gets messy, so I abandon that idea and move on to placing vents instead. Still placing ribs and plates...

Adding handle geometry with backplate and grip, then placing horizontal straps with hinge spheres and plank seam lines, finally defining the door and frame boxes along the z-axis...

Still working out the cap polygon coordinates...
